Not more than 30 years, as on the cut-off date 15/07/2026. Government servants get up to 5 years relaxation under Central Govt instructions. Contractual employees of the same department get a one-time relaxation equal to their contractual service, up to 5 years, if they worked at least 120 days in that year (Services Dept OM F.19(11)/2015/S-IV/1751-1756 dated 11/06/2019). General relaxation under Para 7: SC/ST 5 yrs; OBC 3 yrs; PwBD 10 yrs; PwBD+SC/ST 15 yrs; PwBD+OBC 13 yrs. Departmental candidates with 3 years of continuous regular service get up to 5 yrs for Group B posts. Ex-Servicemen get military service plus 3 years, up to age 55. Widow/divorcee and MSP relaxations apply to Group C only, so they do not apply to this Group B post.

current.value: Essential, any one of: (1) BCA from a recognized university; OR graduation in Computer Science from a recognized university, with CS studied as a main subject in all years; OR BE/B.Tech (Computer Science/IT) from a recognized university; OR graduation in any subject plus the 'A' level course from DOEACC, Ministry of ICT, Govt of India. Note: the Competent Authority may relax qualifications, with reasons recorded, for candidates who are otherwise well qualified. Desirable: NIL. Experience: NIL.

Row 3 of Para 4 covers post codes 41/26, 42/26, 43/26 and 44/26: One Tier (Technical/Teaching), exam code I-T-T, 2 hours, 200 MCQs for 200 marks, no descriptive paper, grand total 200. Section A has 100 one-mark MCQs: General Awareness; General Intelligence & Reasoning Ability; Arithmetical & Numerical Ability; Test of Hindi Language & Comprehension; Test of English Language & Comprehension, 20 marks each. Section B has 100 one-mark MCQs (100 marks) 'from the subject concerned including questions on teaching methodology/ B.Ed.' Negative marking: 0.25 deducted for each wrong 1-mark MCQ. Questions are bilingual (Hindi and English) except the language sections. Scores are normalized if required (Notice 11.07.2018).
current.sourceTitle: Advertisement No. 03/2026, Para 4 Examination Scheme and Notes (pp.27-31)
current.note: DSSSB reserves the right to change the scheme before the exam. Re-evaluation is not available.

current.value: Minimum qualifying marks: General/EWS 40%, OBC (Delhi) 35%, SC/ST/PwBD 30%, and ESM 5% lower than their category, with a floor of 30%. For One Tier Technical/Teaching, the minimum applies only to Section B (the domain subject). Section A has no minimum, but the minimum also applies to the cumulative marks. The final merit list uses Section A + Section B combined. Ties are broken by higher Section B marks, then older age, then alphabetical first name.
current.sourceTitle: Advertisement No. 03/2026, Para 4 note and Para 5
current.note: This differs from the 2017 TGT notice, which required qualifying in Sections A and B separately. The Section-B-only rule is not new in 2026: it already applied under Advt 08/22 (39/22) and Advt 02/23 (70/23).

pattern.qualifyingRule2026: Minimum qualifying marks (Gen/EWS 40%, OBC-Delhi 35%, SC/ST/PwBD 30%, ESM -5% with a 30% floor) apply to Section B and to the cumulative total. Section A has no minimum. Merit is A+B combined, normalized if needed.
changesVsOlderRules: 2017 TGT notice (28/07/2017): candidates had to qualify Sections A and B separately. From Advt 08/22 (and 02/23, 03/2026), the minimum applies only to Section B plus the cumulative total. This is not new in 2026.
Section counts, marks, duration and negative marking match the 2017, 2021 and 2023 scheme notices; no 2026 change to the structure was found.

The 41/26 Section B syllabus (the 32-unit list) differs from the NDMC 70/23 TGT CS indicative syllabus, which follows a CBSE-style topic list (Computer Systems & Organization, Python, Society Law & Ethics, etc.).

historyFacts.value: DSSSB notice No. F.4(100)/2012/P&P/NES/DSSSB/805-810 dated 28/07/2017 (Board resolution P&P/2017/17 dated 17/07/2017) set the TGT exam: one MCQ paper of 2 hours. Section A: 100 one-mark MCQs 'as per existing examination scheme', 100 marks. Section B: 100 one-mark MCQs from the subject 'including questions on teaching methodology/B.Ed.', 100 marks. Candidates had to qualify Sections A and B separately; merit used the aggregate.
historyFacts.sourceTitle: Notice: examination scheme prescribed by DSSSB for the post of TGT
historyFacts.note: Listed on https://dsssb.delhi.gov.in/dsssb/new-examination-and-interview-scheme. The separate-qualification rule was later replaced: the 2022-2026 advertisements apply minimum qualifying marks only to Section B plus the cumulative total.

sectionA.title: SYLLABUS: I-T-T One Tier (Technical / Teaching) 200 Marks — Section A

parts.subject: General Awareness
parts.text: Current events, everyday observation, History, Polity, Constitution, Sports, Art & Culture, Geography, Economics, Everyday Science, Scientific Research, National/International Organizations/Institutions.

parts.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
parts.text: Analogy, Classification, Series, Coding-Decoding, Blood Relations, Direction Sense, Logical Venn Diagrams, Alphabet Test, Sitting Arrangements, Mathematical Operations, Arithmetical Reasoning, Missing character, Number/Ranking/Time Sequence, Eligibility Test, Syllogism, Statement-Arguments/Assumptions/Courses of action/Conclusions, Deriving Conclusion, Assertion-Reason, Punch Lines, Situation Reaction, Cause and Effect, Analytical Reasoning.

parts.subject: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability
parts.text: Number Systems incl. Simplification, Decimals, Data Interpretation, Fractions, LCM, HCF, Ratio & Proportion, Percentage, Average, Profit & Loss, Discount, Simple & Compound Interest, Mensuration, Time & Work, Time & Distance, Tables & Graphs, Pie/Line/Bar charts, Venn Diagrams.

parts.subject: English Language
parts.text: Vocabulary, grammar, sentence structure, synonyms, antonyms and their correct usage; comprehension.

parts.subject: Hindi Language
parts.text: शब्दावली, व्याकरण, वाक्य संरचना, पर्यायवाची, विलोम और उनका सही प्रयोग; बोधगम्यता (vocabulary, grammar, sentence structure, synonyms, antonyms, correct usage).
